## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert is an odd-looking man with an ungainly figure, stooping shoulders, and kindly brown eyes. He has worn a full, soft brown beard since the age of twenty, along with long iron-gray hair that reaches his shoulders and has grown noticeably grayer over the course of a year.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P34](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P26](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0026)_

## Personality

Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet, shy, and patient man who hates being around strangers or going to places where he might have to speak. He holds a deep dread of women, with the exception of [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Rachel, and feels a mortal dread of little girls. Despite his quiet nature, he is wise, kind, and good-natured, proving to be a sympathetic listener who enjoys talkative people willing to converse without expecting him to respond. Although argument is not his strong point, he is known for clinging to his opinions with incredible silent persistency, such as when he desired to keep [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). He is notably lenient and forgiving, offering love and sympathy to those around him without ever scolding.

## History

Matthew Cuthbert lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), having grown up when the farm's new house was built, and habitually wore a full brown beard since the age of twenty. Shy by nature, Matthew dreaded all women with the exception of his sister [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md). When he drove to [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he unexpectedly found a young girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) instead. Unable to refuse her, he brought her home, and after [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) initially insisted on returning [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to the asylum, Matthew successfully advocated for keeping her. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) was later confined to her room following a conflict with Mrs. [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), Matthew secretly visited her to persuade her to apologize so she could rejoin the household. Over the next few years, he consistently supported [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), giving her gifts such as a calf, chocolates, and a stylish puffed-sleeve dress he procured with Mrs. Lynde's assistance. Matthew took great pride in Anne's academic achievements, assuring her before her departure for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy) that he was prouder of her than of a dozen boys. Shortly after Anne's graduation, Matthew suffered a fatal collapse upon reading of the Abbey Bank's failure, leaving [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to mourn his passing.

## Quotes

> "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P3](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0003)

> "It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P13](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0013)

> "That’s right—that’s right, Anne. But don’t tell Marilla I said anything about it. She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P19](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0019)

> “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P25](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0025)

> “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I’ll do all the chores.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P38](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0038)
